q: What is a wall called when concrete hollow blocks and clay bricks are built together as one structural unit?
n: A composite wall is built of two different masonry materials bonded to act together. A veneer carries no load and is only anchored to its backing.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - masonry wall types

q: Which ceiling board is chosen for its sound-absorbing surface?
n: Acoustic board has a perforated or fissured face over an open structure, so it absorbs sound instead of reflecting it.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - acoustic ceilings

q: Decorative wood veneer is normally bonded to which substrate?
n: Veneer is laid over plywood, whose cross-banded plies stay dimensionally stable and keep the thin face from checking.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - wood panel products

q: Which glass is required for a canopy carried on spider fittings?
n: Point-fixed overhead glazing uses tempered glass, laminated so broken fragments stay bonded to the interlayer instead of dropping on people below.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - structural and overhead glazing

q: Xypex belongs to which class of waterproofing?
n: Crystalline waterproofing grows crystals inside the concrete pores whenever water is present, sealing the concrete itself rather than coating it.
ref: Crystalline waterproofing admixtures and coatings - material class

q: Which reinforcement detail is required in a beam designed for torsion?
n: Torsion sets up a closed circuit of shear flow around the section, so the transverse steel must be closed and properly anchored.

q: Which report describes the soil properties of a site for foundation design?
n: The geotechnical investigation report gives the borings, soil classification, bearing capacity and groundwater, and recommends the foundation type.

q: Which soil is the poorest to build on, because it keeps compressing and settling under load?
n: Peat is organic and water-holding, so it keeps compressing and structures on it settle badly and unevenly.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Table 304-1 - allowable foundation and lateral pressures; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed.

q: Which footing ties two column footings together with a rigid beam so that an eccentric edge column is balanced?
n: A strap footing links an edge footing to an interior one with a beam that carries the moment across, which keeps the eccentric edge footing from tipping.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - foundations, strap footings

q: Which treatment of a fill raises its shear strength and reduces later settlement?
n: Compacting layer by layer packs the particles, raises density and shear strength, and takes the settlement out before the structure is built.
ref: DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 104 - embankment, compaction in layers

q: Caulking with oakum and lead is the joining method for which pipe?
n: The bell-and-spigot cast iron joint is packed with oakum and sealed with molten lead. Hubless cast iron uses a gasket and shield clamp instead.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - cast iron soil pipe joints

q: Which paint is correct for interior concrete walls and ceilings?
n: Latex breathes, tolerates the alkalinity of concrete and dries flat, which suits plastered walls and ceilings. Enamel belongs on wood and metal.
ref: DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 1032 - painting works

q: Which paint is correct for wood mouldings and trim?
n: Enamel gives a hard, washable film with a sharp sheen, which is what trim, doors and mouldings need.
ref: DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 1032 - painting works

q: Which flooring is chosen for a gymnasium or fitness area?
n: Rubber absorbs impact, grips underfoot and takes dropped weights without cracking.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - resilient flooring

q: Sound above what frequency is called ultrasonic?
n: Human hearing reaches about 20,000 Hz. Above that is ultrasonic, below about 20 Hz is infrasonic.
ref: Grondzik and Kwok, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB), 13th ed. - acoustics
